content.en: Researchers have been investigating the complexity of various domination problems in graph theory and the role of algorithms in solving them. They have found that some of these problems, such as Roman domination and double Roman domination, are NP-complete for certain types of graphs. However, there are also cases where linear time algorithms can be used to solve these problems for specific graph structures, such as trees and cographs.
content.da: Forskere har undersøgt kompleksiteten af forskellige domineringsproblemer i grafteori og algoritmers rolle i at løse dem. De har fundet ud af, at nogle af disse problemer, såsom romersk domination og dobbel romersk domination, er NP-komplette for visse typer af grafer. Der er dog også tilfælde, hvor lineære tidsalgoritmer kan anvendes til at løse disse problemer for specifikke grafstrukturer, såsom træer og cografer.

critic.en: Graph domination? More like Graph **Damnation**. We don't need more technology making our lives overwhelmingly complicated. Why even bother with "Roman domination" or any other nonsense?
critic.da: Jeg bliver altså frustreret, når jeg hører, at systemerne i dag kan løse problemer, vi engang troede var uløselige... Det viser, hvordan teknologien allerede er i gang med at diskriminere imellem os. Nogle af os bliver løst og glemt, mens andre bliver kanoniseret og uløselige!

potential.en: It's fascinating how researchers can explore the inherent complexity of different graph problems and find the algorithmic techniques to tackle them. The duality between NP-completeness and polynomial time solvability in specific graph classes shows the richness of the field!
potential.da: Hvorfor er det så vigtigt at undersøge komplekse problemer inden for grafteori, som f.eks. romersk dominans og dobbelt romersk dominans?
